title: Why People Who Hate Cannabis And/Or Think It Is Dangerous Should Be Opposed To Prohibition

content_html_sanitized:
For years now, I have argued that cannabis prohibition is a “counterproductive fraud”, but apparently I have not done a very good job of it. So, let’s start at the beginning.

 

In 1937, when the Federal Marihuana Tax Act was passed by Congress, almost no one had ever heard of it, including the members of Congress who voted for it.

 

“Sam Rayburn of Texas explained, “It has something to do with something that is called marihuana. I believe it is a narcotic of some kind.”

 

By 2023, approximately 61.8 million Americans had used marijuana in the past year.

 

And there are hundreds of millions more around the world.

 

When cannabis did reemerge in the 1960s, it was discovered by the most culturally influential people in recent human history, rock stars!

 

Then it became identified with the youth counterculture

and opposition to the very unpopular Vietnam war, and Richard Nixon. Great marketing!!!

 

It was also clear that the marijuana laws were — and still are— disproportionately enforced against racial minorities, which further eroded their credibility.

 

During this time, there was also a massive “drug education” campaign, but it was really designed more to support prohibition, rather than be persuasive to children. DARE became a joke. The term “Forbidden Fruit” somehow comes to mind.

From 2000 Teen Who Hacked DARE Website To Be Tried As Adult. How They Protect Our Youth!

 

When it became clear that it had some medical uses, the government began a major campaign claiming that it did not, and even persecuted AIDS and cancer patients, and even disabled veterans, further undermining their credibility.

 

If cannabis had been sold as medicine to seniors, it would certainly have been less attractive to adolescents.

 

Then when improved breeding and horticultural methods resulted in higher levels of THC, the Prohibitionists and their useful idiots in the media began saying that it was so much “stronger”, therefore more dangerous, than it used to be (even including references to “Woodstock”, the iconic music festival).

 

Of course, “stronger” means better to the typical “criminal” (a cannabis user, especially adolescents, who really don’t believe anything that they have been told about it, with good reason.)

See The Perils of Potent Pot Party Line: Blaming Marijuana Legalization for Increase in THC Levels

 

Then there’s the strawman argument that “marijuana isn’t harmless like everyone thought back in the sixties.” Instead of saying that everything can be overdone, and affects everyone differently, the Prohibitionist establishment, NIDA and the DEA have kept up the “latest research”, funded by the Prohibitionists. That has clearly undermined their credibility, especially with the Internet warning every day that everything causes everything.

 

Then there are the psychiatric rehab rackets.

See Politicized Psychiatry and the Rehab Rackets

 

But the most compelling reasons for taking cannabis out the black market are simply public health and safety.

 

If cannabis is dangerous, it is more dangerous when you don’t know what the THC percent is in contraband. Or if it really is cannabis, not a synthetic.

The Problems with “Synthetic Cannabis” Begin With Its Name

 

And if you don’t want an adolescent to use it, it is better to have it sold by licensed dealers than street dealers.

 

And if you don’t want it to be a “gateway drug” then it is better to separate the markets from hard drugs.

 

And if you don’t want to subsidize organized crime or terrorists, then don’t give them a monopoly.

 

And if you want to have more police resources to deal with criminals and terrorists, don’t waste them on weed.

 

And if you don’t want smoking to be a public nuisance, provide places to smoke and gather socially and share interests.

 

If the law was a magic wand, then maybe you would want to wave it and make cannabis disappear, but that hasn’t worked for the last ninety years. Instead, consider sensible legislation and don’t over tax it or over regulate it and make the problems created by prohibition go away.
